messages.text: Brilliant Sun Goddess in class of her own at Breeders' Cup

metadata.summary: Sun Goddess confirmed herself as a two-year-old out of the ordinary with a clear-cut win Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf at Keeneland.
metadata.content: Breeders' Cup: Sun Goddess in class of her own with Juvenile Fillies Turf win at Keeneland as Libertango takes Juvenile Turf Sprint | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breeders' Cup: Sun Goddess in class of her own with Juvenile Fillies Turf win at Keeneland as Libertango takes Juvenile Turf Sprint Sun Goddess capped off a memorable two-year-old season with a fourth success at the top level with a scintillating display in the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf on a winning night for the European raiders at Keeneland; Libertango won the opening Juvenile Turf Sprint Friday 30 October 2026 22:08, UK Image: Sun Goddess, ridden by Ryan Moore, wins the John Deere Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf at Keeneland Sun Goddess confirmed herself as a two-year-old out of the ordinary with a clear-cut win Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf at Keeneland. Seen by many as the banker of the two-day meeting, she already had three Group Ones in Europe to her credit but she had to contend with the journey to America and stall nine. However, Ryan Moore got her out of the stalls sharply and across to the inside in the perfect position just behind the leader whereas her main market rival, Francis-Henri Graffard's Amusingly, had to settle at the rear of the field. As soon as Moore kicked clear early in the straight the race was over as a contest and once again it was left to Joseph O'Brien's Green Empress to chase her home, the fourth time she has been second to the winner this year. messages.text: Furious Komatsu dismisses 'nonsense' reports of Bearman demanding £5m salary

metadata.summary: Haas boss Ayao Komatsu has furiously dismissed reports claiming that contract extension talks with Oliver Bearman are being held up by the British driver demanding a £5m annual salary.
metadata.content: Oliver Bearman: Haas boss Ayao Komatsu furiously dismisses reports claiming British driver is demanding £5m annual salary | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Oliver Bearman: Haas boss Ayao Komatsu furiously dismisses reports claiming British driver is demanding £5m annual salary Watch every Mexico City GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 9pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday Friday 30 October 2026 21:47, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu has dismissed speculation suggesting Oliver Bearman will be leaving the team Haas boss Ayao Komatsu has furiously dismissed reports claiming that contract extension talks with Oliver Bearman are being held up by the British driver demanding a £5m annual salary. Both Bearman and Komatsu have expressed confidence in recent weeks that a deal will be done to extend the 21-year-old's current contract, which expires at the end of the 2026 season. With Haas having already announced the signing of Bearman's fellow Ferrari junior Rafael Camara to replace Esteban Ocon next season, the lack of confirmation on his own future has led to speculation over what the issues are that are holding up the deal. metadata.summary: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was fastest from champion-elect Kimi Antonelli in first practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Mexico City GP: Charles Leclerc dominates first practice from Kimi Antonelli as Ferrari show strong pace | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mexico City GP: Charles Leclerc dominates first practice from Kimi Antonelli as Ferrari show strong pace Ferrari's Charles Leclerc put down a statement time in first practice to be more than half a second clear of the field, including Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli; watch every session of the Mexico City GP live on Sky Sports F1, with Friday's second practice at 10pm Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Friday 30 October 2026 20:05, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Charles Leclerc set the quickest lap time during the first practice session at the Mexico City GP Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was fastest from champion-elect Kimi Antonelli in first practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Leclerc was 0.659s quicker than Antonelli to underline the expectation that Ferrari will be strong at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez due to their small turbo working well at high altitude. Lewis Hamilton was fourth after a scruffy soft-tyre lap but will be buoyed by his team-mate's pace as Ferrari look to win only their third race of the season. metadata.summary: You would be forgiven for wondering how much longer Michael Carrick will remain in the Manchester United dugout.

You would be forgiven for wondering how much longer Michael Carrick will remain in the Manchester United dugout. A run of eight games without a win has left Carrick searching for answers, with the performances raising as many questions as the results. The energy and organisation of his interim spell last season has been replaced by a team struggling to find their identity. Chelsea away is next on Saturday.
